name: Taylor — Poetry and Authored Images
description: The authored corpus whole: poems that return to their speaker, the two roads of two, the prose images that retain the relation they expose, and the keeping of the opening in the form.

scenes.name: A word that can return to its speaker
scenes.character: Checkmate asks to be played again; mystery deepens as the relation becomes articulate; the One knows the One through no-one; 0 is the One, 1 the All.

entities.name: checkmate — and "Another game?"
the husk — what comes back when knowing fixes on its object
"The 0 is the One, the 1 is the All!" — FT-P04
the institutions which must not devour the humanity that made and makes them (FT-P07)

text.kicker: #0–#1 · the Personal Poetry Corpus: ten earlier works, P0–P5, seven journal works
text.title: A word that can return to its speaker
text.italic: The poems demonstrate returns in different bodies: play reopening after checkmate, knowing restored to its conjugal joy, the One keeping its offices through changed case.

text.body: The corpus gives twenty-three individual works: ten earlier works, P0→P5, seven journal works. FT-P01 plays to checkmate and asks to play again. FT-P02 gives the Unknown relative knowability and removes final possession from the Known — the husk is what an exclusive focus spits back. FT-P03 passes 'it takes one to know one' through three changes of case. FT-P07 dreams institutions that respect their constitution.

Occurrences: checkmate and the replayed game (FT-P01, #5→0); the husk (FT-P02); the three cases of one (FT-P03); the 0/1 line (FT-P04, developed at #1); the devouring institution (FT-P07, returned at #4's black sun).

scenes.name: Two roads, six works, and the return through the loop
scenes.character: 2 → (−1)+1 = 0 beside 2 → 0/1 → 00,01,10,11 + 0,1 = 4+2; P3's productive play answered by P4's severance; P5's word that points where no word can stand.

P0 — 4+2: the four pairings with the generating two retained
P3 — two through the Two Ones, ring around the Rosie, falling down through the loop

text.kicker: #2 · FT-P11–P16; the complementary lean of P3/P4 (human-amplified: yes)
text.title: Two roads, six works, and the return through the loop
text.italic: The numerical poem demonstrates the fate of relation under two operations: addition cancelling the poles, or the Two Ones generating their four pairings with the generating two retained.

text.body: FT-P11 is the fork: 2 → (−1)+1 = 0, and 2 → 0/1 → 4+2 — relation's fate under two operations. FT-P12: where two see the common root, our powers grow. FT-P14 carries two through the Two Ones — playing itself apart to 4+2, falling down through the loop. FT-P15: we forgot that one really is two; humility before precision. FT-P16 finds the limit — so, to speak.
Occurrences: the fork rows (FT-P11); the common root (FT-P12); the loop's fall (FT-P14, #5→0); the sealed sky and open sky (FT-P15, #4's frame images); the three pauses (FT-P16).

text.kicker: #4 · Draft 3; the Singh/Abhinavagupta encounter; the core theorem; the copula programme
text.title: Images that retain the relation they expose
text.italic: Each image demonstrates one operation: definition acknowledging its limit, a frame that opens rather than encloses, manifold interpretation answerable to its object, context holding reversals, fracture kept as recognition's means.

text.body: The prose images give material operations: the fish describing the water it lives in, the faithful definition succeeding by acknowledging its limit; cage and window both needing the frame; the kaleidoscope's word a local orbital centre (returns-to Vāk); the Necker cube's context holding its readings; the kept fracture authenticating relation across absence; the erased dots — form kept, reciprocity gone (A13).
Occurrences: the fish and the definition (Draft 3, A01); the cage/window (C21); the orbital word (A06); the cube's context (A04, A22); the kept counterpart (A23); the erased dots (A13).

scenes.name: The black sun and the radiating star
scenes.character: Capture receives energy without answering circulation; the Work/Play inversion; four rings of depth; the attention sequence from cynicism to blankness — and the star that gives outward.

entities.name: the black sun — intake without renewal
the four rings — Neptune's distance, Jupiter's gravity, Mercury's fixers, the corona's mutual exposure
the radiating star — what reaches the centre becoming available outward
cynicism → exhaustion → blankness — the field ready for re-inscription
city · bomb · surveillance · counterfeit — three distinct failures (destruction, capture, forged source)

text.kicker: #4 · the adopted social-power unit; A29, A24, A25, A32 (human-amplified: yes for the adopted operations)
text.title: The black sun and the radiating star
text.italic: The image demonstrates capture against circulation: the public work channel becomes performance while effective decision moves into concealed play — and the return must let work, attention and judgement come back as generative capacity.

text.body: Attention and labour move toward a centre; the public edge presents work done for others, and the power to decide its use sits deeper. The black sun gathers capture: energy received without answering circulation. The radiating star changes the destination: what reaches the centre becomes available outward. The Work/Play inversion runs over four concentric rings — Neptune, Jupiter, Mercury, corona. Cynicism, exhaustion, blankness: a field ready for re-inscription.
Occurrences: the black sun's intake and the star's radiance (#4); the four rings (#4); the attention sequence (#4); the city/bomb/surveillance/counterfeit distinctions (#4, returned at #5→0).

scenes.name: Keeping the opening in the form
scenes.character: Each ending qualifies its work: the replayed game, the loop's fall, the returned shoe. The four operators of alterity; the recursive Bimba office; the way back to the particular words.

entities.name: God as Other — source exceeding possession
shadow as other-self · friend as my-self's-other · alien/enemy as externalised uncertainty
the returned shoe — "Let the shoe fit / But return it" (FT-P23)
recursive Bimba — a reference genuinely occupying the local original's office, pratibimba in the wider relation

text.kicker: #5→0 · A11, A01, A06; Neumann's shared structuration; the compilation's order and corrections
text.title: Keeping the opening in the form
text.italic: The whole demonstrates return as more than theme: play beginning again, the six routes falling through the loop, the fitting shoe returned — each ending qualifying the work that precedes it.

text.body: Return is exact here: play begins again after checkmate; the six routes fall through their loop; the shoe must still be returned. God, shadow, friend, alien — four offices of alterity meeting in one encounter (A27, without becoming four character classes). Bimba keeps contextual office and wider dependence together. Corrections stand beside their texts; the way back to the particular words stays open.
Occurrences: the returned shoe (FT-P23, #5→0); the loop's fall (FT-P14, #2, #5→0); the four operators (#4, #5→0); the authorial sequence corrections (FT-P19, FT-P21, FT-P22 as stated instructions).
